title: Kit Carson Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Kit Carson wells have a 45 ft median depth and typical finished well costs of $7,600-$14,500.
h1: What Wells Are Like Around Kit Carson
intro_html:
If you are buying land or a home near Kit Carson, the local well records point to shallow wells in plains sediments and sedimentary rock. The median reported depth is 45 feet, and the middle half runs from 38 to 52 feet. Reported yields are also strong, with a 15.0 gpm median among the limited number of wells that report pumping results.

These figures describe permitted wells within 5 miles of Kit Carson in Cheyenne County. They are useful for planning, but they do not guarantee what a new well will find on a particular parcel. Confirm the permit status, water right, well construction, and neighboring well performance before you close.

sections.heading: Kit Carson wells are usually shallow
sections.html:
Depth is the clearest local pattern. All recorded wells with a reported depth are under 100 feet. The median is 45 feet, the middle half is 38 to 52 feet, and the deepest well in the records is 81 feet. No recorded wells fall in the 100-300 foot, 300-600 foot, or 600+ foot ranges.

For a driller, that range usually means a bid should be based on a shallow target, with an allowance for variation in local alluvium and plains sedimentary rock. Shallow does not mean automatic. A casing and grout plan still matters, and a nearby well log is more useful than relying on the median alone.

sections.heading: What a Kit Carson well may produce
sections.html:
Only 21 wells in the records report a pump yield, so the yield statistics are a guide rather than a guarantee. Among those reports, the median is 15.0 gpm and the middle half is 7.0 to 15.0 gpm. The records show 57% above 15 gpm, 33% between 5 and 15 gpm, and 10% between 1 and 5 gpm.

No reported wells are under 1 gpm, but the small sample still deserves caution. A buyer should request the well construction report, pump test information, and actual pressure and recovery history. Household demand, stock use, and irrigation needs should be matched to the permitted use, not just to the reported yield.

sections.heading: Water levels around Kit Carson
sections.html:
The 11 reported static water levels have a median depth to water of 38 feet, with the middle half from 30 to 48 feet. That is broadly consistent with the shallow well depths in this plains setting, but it is not a measure of how much water a well can produce while pumping.

The permit record does not provide enough reported water-level observations here to establish a reliable dropping or rising trend by decade. A static level can also change with weather, pumping nearby, and the time since the well was last used. For a purchase, compare the subject well with current measurements from nearby wells and have the pump system checked under load.

sections.heading: Kit Carson permit history and local drillers
sections.html:
Kit Carson has 140 wells in the Colorado DWR permit records, with 86 recorded as constructed and 91 reporting a total depth. Permits appear across several decades: 7 in the 1950s, 7 in the 1960s, 14 in the 1970s, 8 in the 1980s, 7 in the 1990s, 1 in the 2000s, 28 in the 2010s, and 7 in the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2024.

The most active names in these records are Kemp's Well Service (Kemp, George), with 16 wells; Authorized (Pe, Pg), with 14; and Eastwood Drilling (Eastwood, Francis), with 8. Treat the list as permit history, not a current availability list.

sections.heading: Planning a new well near Kit Carson
sections.html:
For the local ground conditions, the drilling model uses a typical rate of $35-$55 per foot. At the 45-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $1,600-$2,500. A finished well, including the pump, tank, trenching, and electrical, is modeled at about $7,600-$14,500.

Those figures are planning ranges, not a fixed quote. Access, casing and grout requirements, power distance, trench conditions, pump sizing, water testing, and an unexpectedly poor hole can change the final price. Ask for a written bid that separates drilling from completion and identifies what happens if the hole is dry or the yield is below the intended use.

sections.heading: Risks to check before buying a lot
sections.html:
The local records name an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer for 123 wells, Alluvial for 7, and Ogallala for 2. Fractured material can be unpredictable even where nearby wells perform well. Confirm the well's permitted use: the recorded mix is 59% stock, 26% domestic or household, 11% monitoring, and 2% irrigation.

Water quality deserves separate testing. The mapping shows 33 PFAS sampling or contamination sites within about 10 miles, with no historic mine features and no EPA Superfund or cleanup sites mapped. Test the existing well, inspect septic setbacks and drainfield space, and confirm the lot can support the planned home, access, utility trenching, and replacement septic system.

sections.heading: Buying or building near Eads and Cheyenne Wells
sections.html:
Start with the exact parcel, not the area average. Pull the DWR permit and construction record, check the static level and pump performance, and compare neighboring wells before making an offer. The records around Kit Carson are shallow overall, but a shallow well can still have a damaged casing, poor grout, contamination, or a pump that cannot meet the home's demand.

For a new build, verify the well permit and allowed use before designing the house and septic system. Nearby reference points include Eads, Cheyenne Wells, Brandon, Arapahoe, and Sheridan Lake, but conditions can change from parcel to parcel. A licensed driller and septic professional should review access, setback constraints, water testing, and the construction budget before excavation begins.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Kit Carson, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth near Kit Carson is 45 feet, and the middle half runs from 38 to 52 feet. Every recorded well with a depth is under 100 feet. The deepest record is 81 feet. These figures cover permitted wells within 5 miles and should guide planning, not replace a site-specific drilling review.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Kit Carson?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $35-$55 per foot. At the 45-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $1,600-$2,500. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $7,600-$14,500. Actual bids can change with access, casing, grout, power distance, and water production.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Kit Carson?
faq.a: Among the 21 local wells that report a pump yield, the median is 15.0 gpm and the middle half is 7.0-15.0 gpm. The records show 57% above 15 gpm, 33% from 5 to 15 gpm, and 10% from 1 to 5 gpm. A pump test is still important because the sample is limited.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Kit Carson?
faq.a: Well depth and yield do not establish drinking-water safety. The mapped area has 33 PFAS sampling or contamination sites within about 10 miles, so test an existing or new well for PFAS and other appropriate contaminants. Review the well construction and septic system, and use a qualified laboratory before relying on the water for household use.

faq.q: Are wells in Kit Carson likely to go dry?
faq.a: The available records do not establish a dry-well rate or a reliable water-level trend. Reported static water levels have a 38-foot median, with the middle half from 30 to 48 feet, but only 11 wells report that measurement. Check neighboring well history, current static level, pump recovery, and the permitted use before buying or building.
